We’re based right here in Portage County, we know the streets around East Garfield Road, and we maintain the same kind of homes you live in.As an exterior contractor in Aurora, OH, we handle roofing, siding, gutters, fencing, decks, brickwork, and home additions under one roof. That means one trusted crew for the whole home — not five different numbers to call.By Johnny, Founder & Owner of Alt & Alt, LLC · 20+ Years Serving Northeast OhioLicensed & Insured · A+ BBB Rated · Owens Corning · GAF · CertainTeed Certified Start My Free Consultation Part of the Aurora Neighborhood, Not Passing ThroughThere’s a real difference between a contractor who just drives through your city and one who’s part of it. We’re the second kind.We’ve worked on classic mid-century homes and newer estate developments across the city. That range matters, because a roof or a foundation detail on an older home isn’t handled the same way as on a new one. Two decades in Portage County means we already know what each Aurora home needs.Being local also means we answer fast. When a storm rolls through near Aurora’s historic downtown and nearby Sunny Lake Park, we’re already close by — not routing a crew in from another county. Get a Free Quote Aurora Winters and Storms Test Every ExteriorAurora weather is tougher on homes than people expect, and it adds up year after year.Lake-effect snow loads the roof for weeks. Freeze-thaw cycles work moisture into every crack, joint, and shingle seam. Summer brings hail and hard storms, and the mature tree canopy near Aurora’s historic downtown and nearby Sunny Lake Park drops debris into gutters all fall.We build and repair with all of that in mind — deeper footings, better flashing, and materials rated for exactly these conditions. Our storm damage repair Aurora service also steps in fast after severe weather, documenting damage and handling the insurance claim for you.The Aurora Services We Provide, Start to FinishMost Aurora homeowners would rather have one team they trust than a list of separate specialists. We cover the whole home, inside and out.RoofingAurora is upscale and green — communities like Aurora Shores, Walden, and the homes around Barrington are set among lakes, ponds, and golf-course fairways, often on generous wooded lots. That means larger, more architecturally detailed roofs under real tree cover. As your roofing contractor in Aurora, we handle those bigger replacements and storm repairs with the ventilation and algae-resistant detailing all that shade calls for, and we back every job with manufacturer and workmanship warranties.SidingAurora’s many lakeside and pond-side lots carry a moisture load, and its upscale homes present a lot of finished elevation to keep looking right. Our siding work — vinyl, insulated, fiber-cement — leads with flashing every opening so water stays outside, and on these larger homes we treat color and profile consistency across a big facade as part of the craft. In gated and HOA communities, we also make sure the product and color meet the community’s standards.FencingAurora issues its own permits through its building department at 129 West Pioneer Trail — not through Portage County — and its gated and HOA communities add strict rules of their own about what you can build. We reconcile all of it before a post goes in. On the lakeside and golf-course lots, we set posts 32 inches down past frost, concreted so nothing shifts, in wood, vinyl, aluminum, or chain-link, with the moisture-exposed wood properly sealed.GuttersWooded, water-adjacent Aurora lots combine a heavy leaf load with ground that’s already damp, and a big home overwhelms an undersized gutter fast. We form seamless gutters on-site, pitch them to move real volume, guard the shaded runs, and size downspouts to the roof so a hard storm gets carried well away from the foundation rather than pooling on a lakeside lot.DecksLakeside and golf-course lots in Aurora Shores, Walden, and Barrington are made for a good deck — and the water-adjacent, sometimes sloped ground makes footings and the ledger connection critical. We dig to frost depth, flash the ledger so the house stays dry, and build multi-level or elevated decks that make the most of a lake or fairway view. Composite, pressure-treated, or a rehab of an aging deck, with extra sealing where moisture runs high.BrickworkUpscale Aurora homes suit substantial masonry — brick and stone patios, outdoor fireplaces, tall chimneys, columns — and freeze-thaw, sped along by the area’s moisture, works at the mortar over time. We build new masonry laid clean and sealed against the cycle, and tuckpoint joints that have begun to open before water gets deeper into a wall or chimney. Work scaled and finished to suit a high-end property.Additions & RemodelsAurora homeowners build for the long haul and for the setting — additions with big windows on the water, sunrooms facing a fairway, whole-home remodels. We match roofline, siding, and finishes so the new work reads as original across a large elevation, and we permit through the City of Aurora’s own building department while meeting any gated- or HOA-community standards. From framing to the final walkthrough, one accountable crew stays on it start to finish.Our Straightforward Way of WorkingWe keep every Aurora project simple, honest, and on your schedule. ## Insulation Services

Struggling with high energy bills and uncomfortable temperatures at home? Our Fiberglass Blow-In Insulation services may be the very solution you’ve been searching for! At Summit Building & Roofing, we provide Fiberglass Blow-In Insulation to seal gaps, improve energy efficiency, and create a more comfortable home for you and your family.

Why Choose Fiberglass Blow-In Insulation?
✅ Superior Coverage: Reaches every nook and cranny for comprehensive insulation
✅ Energy Savings: Reduces heating and cooling costs (Save up to 25% on your energy bills)

https://www.yicnroofing.com/blog/how-muc.text: ROOFING | ROOF REPLACEMENT10 min readHow Much Does Roof Replacement Cost in Cleveland? (2026 Prices)Cleveland roof replacement costs run $9,000-$18,000 for most homes. Here's the 2026 per-square price breakdown by material, the line items honest estimates include, and how to compare bids.Kevin Stone, Chairman - YICN RoofingJuly 4, 2026Listen to this articleHear a quick audio overview of How Much Does Roof Replacement Cost in Cleveland? (2026 Prices).Your browser does not support the audio player.Most roof replacements in Cleveland cost between $9,000 and $18,000 for a typical single-family home with asphalt shingles. That's the honest, boring answer, and it's the number I'd want first if I were the one with a water stain spreading across my ceiling. In roofing, one "square" covers 100 square feet, and most Cleveland homes measure between 18 and 25 squares. Material choice moves the price more than anything else you control: per square, expect roughly $300 – $500 for basic three-tab shingles, $450 – $800 for architectural shingles (what most of our neighbors choose), and $1,000 – $2,000+ for standing seam metal.Last winter a guy from Old Brooklyn called us after a piece of his ceiling came down in his kid's bedroom — not a stain, a chunk of drywall on the floor, because water had been sitting in his attic for months. He didn't want to talk numbers first. He wanted to know if his family was safe sleeping there that night. That's roofing in Cleveland. So below the price tables, I'll also tell you what our lake-effect winters and spring hail do to roofs that other cities don't deal with, how to read an estimate line by line, and how homeowners around here finance the job without draining a savings account.Key TakeawaysCleveland Price Range: Most single-family roof replacements in Cleveland run $9,000 – $18,000 installed, with the Ohio average re-roof at $8,500 – $13,500.Per-Square Pricing (2026): Architectural shingles cost $450 – $800 per square (100 sq ft); three-tab runs $300 – $500, standing seam metal $1,000 – $2,000+.The Hidden Add-Ons: Tear-off runs $50 – $150 per square, water-damaged decking $75 – $150 per sheet, and permits $50 – $300 depending on your city.Estimate Red Flags: A bid that omits tear-off, dumpster, or permit lines isn't cheap — it's an incomplete scope. Get 2–3 written, itemized estimates.Timeline: Most Cleveland homes are completed in 1 – 3 days, and storm, hail, or wind damage may be covered by insurance while age and wear are not.Quick Answer: Roof Replacement Cost in Cleveland (2026)Most single-family homes: $9,000 to $18,000 installed — Angi's 2026 data pegs the national average at $9,500 – $11,600Per square (100 sq ft) with architectural shingles: $450 – $800Typical timeline: one to three days of workThe three variables that move your quote most: roof size in squares, material choice, and what the tear-off reveals underneathIf your number came back outside that range, the sections below explain why — and which direction is the suspicious one.Why Cleveland Roofs Cost What They CostCleveland isn't Phoenix. Our roofs deal with lake-effect snow, ice dams in January, hail in the spring, and humidity that sits on shingles all summer. A roofer working in Cuyahoga County has to build for freeze-thaw cycles, and that means ice and water shield at the eaves, more nails per shingle in wind zones, and labor time that a warm-climate crew never thinks about.Here's what makes up a typical quote:Cost FactorWhat It CoversTypical Share of Total CostMaterials (shingles, underlayment, flashing)Architectural shingles, ice and water shield, drip edge35–45%LaborTear-off, disposal, install crew30–40%Roof size and pitchSteeper or larger roofs need more time and materialsVaries by homeDecking repairReplacing rotten or water-damaged plywood underneathAdd-on cost if neededPermits and disposalLocal permit fees, dumpster rentalSmall but requiredA homeowner in Parma told us she got three quotes and they were all within a few hundred dollars of each other — the honest ones anyway. The one that came in way lower left out tear-off and dump fees. She found out after she signed. That's a real thing to watch for: a low number that skips the tear-off or the dumpster isn't a deal, it's a surprise bill waiting to happen.Roof Replacement Cost Per Square by Material (2026)Roofers price per "square" — a 10x10 foot section, 100 square feet. Material is the biggest lever you control. Here's what materials run per square in the Cleveland market, installed, based on 2026 national pricing data — Fixr puts the national average roof replacement at about $10,000, and HomeGuide tracks installed asphalt pricing at $300 – $600 per square. Ohio jobs tend to land in the middle of these ranges: our average re-roof runs $8,500 – $13,500.MaterialInstalled Cost Per Square (2026)Expected LifespanThree-tab asphalt shingles$300 – $50015–20 yearsArchitectural asphalt shingles$450 – $80025–30 yearsPremium/designer shingles$800 – $1,600+30–40 yearsStanding seam metal$1,000 – $2,000+40–70 yearsCorrugated/agitated metal panels$500 – $1,20025–40 yearsCedar shake$1,000 – $1,500+20–30 yearsTwo honest notes from the field. First, architectural shingles are what most of our neighbors go with — they hold up better against wind off the lake, and the price gap over three-tab has narrowed. A guy in Lakewood almost went three-tab to save a couple grand until his neighbor pointed out his own three-tab roof was curling at twelve years. Second, if your home has a flat or low-slope section — common on additions, garages, and older Cleveland doubles — that's priced differently, and we cover it in our flat roof replacement guide.Roof Size: What Cleveland Homes Typically PayHome SizeRoof Squares (approx)Estimated Cost Range (Architectural)Small ranch (1,200 sq ft)12–15 squares$7,500 – $11,000Mid-size colonial (2,000 sq ft)20–25 squares$11,000 – $16,000Larger home (2,800+ sq ft)28–35 squares$16,000 – $24,000+Want to ballpark yours without a tape measure? Most homes need roughly one square per 100 square feet of footprint, adjusted for pitch and overhangs — or just use our roofing calculator and have real squares in two minutes.Cleveland Weather Problems That Drive Up CostNortheast Ohio throws a few specific problems at roofs that other regions don't:Ice dams — snow melts off warmer parts of the roof, then refreezes at the edge. That ice backs water up under your shingles. Bad attic insulation makes it worse, and it's incredibly common in the older homes of Cleveland Heights and Shaker Heights.Hail damage — spring storms leave dents in shingles you won't notice from the ground. If a storm just came through, get an inspection before the damage becomes a leak. Our hail damage page covers the claim side.Wind damage — homes closer to the lake, like Rocky River and Bay Village, take a beating off Erie. Loose or lifted shingles are the first sign.Humidity and trapped moisture — a roof with poor ventilation bakes in summer, which ages shingles from the underside and rots decking.None of these automatically mean a full replacement. But if your roof is 15–20 years old and one of these hits, it's usually the thing that tips a homeowner from "patch it" to "replace it."Tear-Off, Decking, and the Line Items Bids SkipThis is where honest estimates get separated from the cheap ones. Ask any contractor who quotes you to put these in writing:Tear-off and disposal — removing one layer of old shingles runs about $50 – $150 per square per 2026 industry data. A second layer (common on older doubles in Cleveland Heights) adds time and weight to the dumpster.Decking replacement — water-damaged plywood gets swapped out at roughly $75 – $150 per sheet. Most homes need a few sheets at most; you don't know until the old roof is off.Steep-pitch surcharge — roofs steeper than 7/12 pitch add labor time; steep-work surcharges typically run 15% – 40% more labor.Permit fees — Cleveland-area cities charge roughly $50 – $300 for a roofing permit depending on jurisdiction; the contractor should pull it and include it in writing.Chimney and flashing detail — re-flashing a chimney or valley work is line-itemed separately on honest bids, not buried in "miscellaneous."A homeowner in North Olmsted budgeted for a straightforward replacement, and the crew found water-damaged plywood around one of her vent pipes. It added a few hundred dollars, not thousands — but it's the kind of thing worth asking about upfront so it's not a surprise.How to Get (and Read) a Roof Replacement Estimate in ClevelandThe estimate is where you find out who you're actually dealing with. Here's the process I'd follow:Inspection first, numbers second. Any contractor who quotes your roof from the driveway, without getting on it, is guessing. A real inspection checks decking, flashing, ventilation, and attic moisture — 20 to 30 minutes.Get two or three written estimates. Not one "special today only" number from a door-knocker. Written, itemized, on company letterhead.Check the line items. Your estimate should show squares, material brand and weight (e.g., 30-year architectural), tear-off layers included, ice and water shield at the eaves, permit fees, and dumpster/disposal. If those aren't listed, ask.Watch the red flags. No tear-off line means it's not included. A big upfront deposit before materials are ordered is illegal territory in some states and bad news everywhere. A quote that's thousands below the other two isn't a bargain — it's a missing scope.Compare warranty terms, not just price. Workmanship warranty length is the honest tell of how much a contractor trusts their own crew.We do free inspections across Cuyahoga, Summit, Medina, and Lorain counties and put every estimate in writing. If you'd like a second opinion on a quote you're already holding, get your estimate here — comparing it against ours is free, and no obligation.Financing a New Roof in ClevelandMost people don't have $12,000 sitting around, and that's normal. Cleveland homeowners typically cover a new roof with:Contractor financing — most roofers (us included) offer plans through financing partners: often $0 down with 0% promotional APR for 12–24 months. One caution: those promos are deferred-interest, meaning if the balance isn't paid before the promo ends, rates of 18%–30% can apply retroactively. Read the fine print.Home equity loans or HELOCs — typically the lowest rates (around 6.5%–8.5% in 2026), with 10-year draw periods on HELOCs. You're borrowing against the house, which is the tradeoff.Personal loans — unsecured, fast approval (24–48 hours), fixed rates around 7.8%–12.5% for good credit, terms of 3–12 years.Homeowners insurance claims — if the damage came from a covered event like a storm or hail, the roof may be mostly covered. Get the inspection and documentation right first.If your roof damage came from a specific storm, get an inspection fast and document everything before you file a claim — insurance adjusters look at timing, and a roof that's been leaking for six months looks different than one hit by last week's storm. Our financing page has actual payment estimates.What Actually Happens on Replacement DayA normal roof replacement in Cleveland takes one to three days, weather depending. The order of operations: tear-off down to the decking, decking inspection and repairs, underlayment and ice/water shield, shingles from the bottom edge up, flashing and ventilation checks around chimneys and valleys, then a magnetic nail sweep and full cleanup. You don't need to leave the house — but move your cars out of the driveway, cover anything fragile in the attic, and keep the kids inside during tear-off.Roof Replacement Cost by Cleveland-Area Neighborhood and CountyPricing doesn't change block to block, but local factors move the number a little:Cleveland Heights & Shaker Heights — older homes, steeper roofs, sometimes multiple old layers that need extra tear-off workLakewood & Rocky River — lake-adjacent, wind exposure; worth asking about wind-rated shinglesParma & Parma Heights — mix of ranch and colonial styles, generally straightforward jobsWestlake & Bay Village — larger newer homes, more roof to coverStrongsville & Medina County — bigger homes on bigger lotsAkron & Summit County — ice dams and hail are the common concernsLorain County — mix of older and newer construction, lake-wind considerationsNot sure if we cover your street? Our locations page lists everywhere we work across Northeast Ohio.Get Your Roof Replacement EstimateEvery number on this page is a range, because every roof is different. The only way to get your number is an inspection — free, written, no obligation. Call YICN Roofing at (937) 756-2124 or request your free estimate online, and we'll get on your roof, not just the driveway.Related Cleveland Roof Replacement GuidesEvery project starts with a budget and a plan. These guides break down the steps that come after the estimate:Wondering whether repair or full replacement makes more sense? Our decision guide walks through the 25% Rule.See exactly how long a roof replacement takes — the full 1-to-3-day timeline, debris and all.Use our 12-step prep checklist to protect landscaping and siding before the crew arrives.Budgeting for permits and HOA approvals in Northeast Ohio? Fees and rules vary by city.Curious how much of the cost a new roof adds back to your home value? Ohio resale data says 57-68%.Frequently Asked QuestionsHow much does roof replacement cost in Cleveland in 2026?How much does a new roof cost per square in Cleveland?What should a roof replacement estimate include?How much do tear-off and decking replacement cost?Will insurance cover roof replacement in Ohio?How long does a roof replacement take in Cleveland?About the Author: Kevin Stone has led Northeast Ohio's premier storm damage roofing contractor, YICN Roofing, for over 12 years, establishing the company as Bedford Heights' most trusted roofing expert. Based at 5420 Mardale Ave, Bedford Heights, OH 44146, Kevin has personally overseen thousands of roof repairs, replacements, and emergency storm responses throughout the 30-mile service area. Northeast Ohio Storm Damage Expertise Kevin's deep understanding of Northeast Ohio's challenging weather patterns—from lake-effect snow and ice dams to severe wind and hail storms—has made YICN Roofing the go-to contractor for insurance claims and emergency roof repairs. His hands-on experience includes major storm responses in Bedford Heights, Cleveland, Akron, and surrounding communities. https://roofingbh.com/services/residenti.text: ServiceResidential Roofing Services in Cleveland & Northeast OhioOne contractor for every stage of your roof's life - not a different crew for every problem.Licensed & InsuredFamily-Owned24/7 Emergency ServiceCall (216) 424-3811Request Free InspectionResidential roofing covers the full life of a roof on a single-family home or small multi-family property - not just the day it gets replaced. BH Roofing works with homeowners across Cleveland and its suburbs at every stage: a first inspection when you buy a house, repairs when something fails, a full replacement when the roof reaches the end of its service life, and maintenance in between to keep small issues from becoming expensive ones. Built Around Cleveland’s Actual Housing Stock Northeast Ohio’s residential roofs aren’t uniform. East-side communities like Shaker Heights and Cleveland Heights carry a lot of pre-WWII Tudors and colonials with older framing and decking conventions. Lakewood’s dense blocks of early-1900s duplexes and foursquares have their own detailing quirks. Newer developments in Solon, Avon, and Strongsville use modern truss framing and different ventilation baselines entirely. We inspect what’s actually there rather than applying one standard spec to every roof. One Contractor, Every Stage A lot of homeowners end up with a different company for inspection, another for repair, and a third for eventual replacement - which means nobody has the full history of the roof. We prefer being the single point of contact across that whole lifecycle, because a repair crew that also handled your original inspection makes better decisions, faster, than one starting from zero. When to Call, Even If Nothing Seems Wrong The best time to have a roof looked at isn’t after a leak starts - it’s during a home purchase, after any significant storm, or on a regular maintenance interval, especially heading into a Northeast Ohio winter. Catching a small flashing gap or early granule loss during a routine check is a fraction of the cost of the interior repair that follows an undetected leak. Getting Started If you’re not sure whether your home needs a repair, a full replacement, or just a check-up, a free inspection is the right starting point. We’ll give you a straight assessment and point you to the specific service that actually fits your roof’s condition. If you’re evaluating a rental property, mixed-use building, or HOA-managed complex instead, see our commercial roofing page - the maintenance and inspection cadence differs meaningfully from a single-family home. Permits and Local Rules Vary More Than Homeowners Expect Roofing permit requirements are broadly similar across Northeast Ohio, but the specifics - inspection scheduling, permit fees, and how quickly an application processes - differ by municipality, and some communities layer on additional review. Historic districts in parts of Cleveland Heights and Lakewood Heights sometimes require sign-off on visible exterior changes, including shingle color or profile, before work begins. HOA-governed developments in newer suburbs can have their own material and color restrictions independent of the municipal permit. We handle the permit filing as part of every project and flag any additional local review early, so it doesn’t surprise you mid-project. What a Fair Estimate Comparison Actually Looks Like Homeowners collecting multiple quotes often compare bottom-line numbers without realizing the scopes underneath aren’t equivalent. A noticeably lower bid often means a shingle-over-shingle install instead of a full tear-off, reduced or missing ice-and-water shield coverage at eaves and valleys, or no attention to attic ventilation as part of the job. None of that shows up in a one-line quote, but all of it shows up in how the roof performs during its first hard winter. We itemize estimates specifically so a homeowner can compare scope against scope, not just price against price. The Full-Lifecycle Advantage in Practice Being the contractor who handled your original inspection, your last repair, and your eventual replacement means decisions get made with actual history rather than guesswork. If we already know a roof’s deck had a soft spot near the chimney from a prior repair, that informs how we scope a later replacement without needing to rediscover it. Homeowners who bounce between different contractors for each need lose that continuity, and it often shows up as either redundant diagnostic work or a missed detail that a company starting from zero wouldn’t have known to check. Housing Stock Across the Suburbs We Serve Beyond the older east-side communities, newer developments in Solon, Avon, and Strongsville present their own residential roofing considerations - modern truss framing, different baseline ventilation specs from the builder, and often larger, more complex rooflines with more valleys and penetrations than older, simpler gable roofs. We adjust our inspection and installation approach to the home’s actual construction era and style rather than a one-size playbook across every project.What's IncludedOne point of contact across inspection, repair, replacement, and maintenanceExperience across the full range of Cleveland-area housing stock, from pre-war city homes to newer suburban buildsStraight guidance on repair versus replacement at every stageWritten estimates and clear scheduling, no bait-and-switch pricingLocal crews who understand Northeast Ohio's specific climate demandsFrequently Asked QuestionsWhat's included under residential roofing versus your other service pages?Residential roofing is the umbrella for everything we do on single-family and small multi-family homes - inspections, repairs, full replacements, and ongoing maintenance. Our other service pages go deeper on specific work (like roof replacement or gutter installation), but residential roofing is the right starting point if you're not sure exactly what your home needs yet.Do you work on older homes with non-standard roof framing?Yes, regularly. A lot of Cleveland's east-side housing stock - Shaker Heights, Cleveland Heights, Lakewood - was built between the 1900s and 1930s with framing and decking conventions that differ from typical modern construction. We inspect the actual structure rather than assuming a modern spec applies, which matters most when planning ventilation or deck repair.How do I know if my home needs an inspection, a repair, or a full replacement?That's exactly what a free inspection answers. Age, extent of any damage, and deck condition all factor in. We give you a straight recommendation, including telling you when a repair is the right call even if a replacement would be a bigger job for us.Do you handle duplexes and small multi-family properties?Yes. Many older Cleveland-area suburbs, particularly Lakewood and parts of Cleveland Heights, have a significant share of duplexes and small multi-family buildings. The roofing principles are the same as single-family homes, though we help coordinate scheduling and scope when multiple owners or units are involved.Do permits work differently for residential roofing across Cleveland-area suburbs?Yes, in the details, even though the underlying code requirements are broadly similar. Individual municipalities and some HOA-governed communities have their own permit application processes, inspection timing, and in a few historic districts, additional review for visible changes like shingle color or profile. We handle the permit filing as part of the project and know the specific requirements for the municipalities we work in most often.What's the biggest mistake homeowners make when choosing a residential roofing contractor?Comparing quotes on price alone without checking that they cover the same scope. A lower number that skips full tear-off, ice-and-water shield at eaves and valleys, or proper ventilation isn't actually a lower price for the same job - it's a smaller job. https://roofingbh.com/services/storm-dam.text: ServiceStorm Damage Roof Repair in Cleveland & Northeast OhioA thorough damage assessment first - so your claim and your repair both reflect what actually happened.Licensed & InsuredFamily-Owned24/7 Emergency ServiceCall (216) 424-3811Request Free InspectionNortheast Ohio sits in a corridor that gets hit by both Lake Erie-driven storm systems and the broader Midwest severe weather pattern - straight-line wind events in summer, hail bands that move through with fast-developing thunderstorms, and occasional derecho-strength gusts that do real damage in a matter of minutes. Storm damage roofing is about assessing what actually happened to your roof, not assuming the worst or, just as often, missing damage that isn’t visible from the ground. What Storm Damage Actually Looks Like Wind damage often shows up as lifted or missing shingle tabs, especially along ridgelines and roof edges where uplift force concentrates. Hail damage is subtler - bruised or fractured shingle mat that doesn’t necessarily leak right away but accelerates granule loss and shortens the roof’s remaining life by years. Debris impact from tree limbs is usually obvious, but the surrounding shingles knocked loose in the same event sometimes aren’t checked closely enough by a fast estimate. Our Assessment Process We inspect the full roof, not just the area you flagged as damaged, because storm force rarely confines itself to one spot. That means checking flashing, ridge caps, and any roof penetrations in addition to the shingle field itself. Every assessment is photographed and documented in a format built to hand directly to an insurance adjuster. Repair or Replace - An Honest Answer Isolated wind damage on an otherwise sound, reasonably current roof is very often a repair. Widespread hail bruising across the whole roof, or storm damage layered onto a roof that was already near end-of-life, points toward replacement being the more sensible long-term call. We’ll tell you which situation you’re in and why, rather than defaulting to whichever answer is more profitable for us. Working Alongside Your Insurance Claim We’re not a public adjuster and we don’t negotiate your policy on your behalf, but the documentation we provide is built to support your claim: clear photos, a written damage summary, and an itemized repair or replacement scope that matches what an adjuster needs to process the claim fairly. See our insurance claims assistance page for more detail on how that process typically works. Storm Damage Follows a Seasonal Pattern Here Northeast Ohio’s storm risk isn’t evenly distributed across the year, and knowing the pattern helps us know what to look for. Summer brings fast-moving thunderstorm complexes, sometimes producing straight-line wind gusts strong enough to lift ridge caps and occasionally hail, often with less warning than a slower-developing system would give. Late fall and winter shift toward sustained lake-effect wind events, capable of significant shingle damage even without any precipitation at all, plus the ice-dam-related failures that show up during winter thaws. An assessment in July looks for different things first than one in January, even though both check the same roof systematically. Damage That Doesn’t Show Up Until Later One of the more underappreciated storm damage patterns is delayed failure - a wind event that loosens a shingle’s fasteners or partially lifts an edge without fully tearing it free. From the ground, and sometimes even on a rushed inspection, that shingle looks intact. It isn’t. The next moderate wind event, sometimes weeks or months later and nowhere near as strong as the original storm, finishes the job. This is exactly why we check ridge caps, edges, and fastening patterns across the whole roof after any significant event, not just the areas with obvious, complete damage - a shingle at 80 percent failure today needs the same attention as one that’s already torn off. Debris Impact Damage: More Than the Obvious Hole A fallen limb or wind-blown debris strike often causes damage well beyond the immediately visible impact point. The surrounding shingles can be knocked loose or cracked by the same impact, and if the strike is heavy enough, the deck sheathing underneath can crack or split even when the roofing material on top looks patchable. We inspect the full area around any debris strike, including from inside the attic where accessible, rather than assuming the visible hole is the entire scope of the damage. Storm Damage Across Different Roof Types A pitched asphalt shingle roof and a flat commercial membrane roof fail differently in the same storm. Wind primarily threatens shingle uplift and ridge cap loss on pitched roofs, while on flat roofs, wind-driven debris and ponding water from a storm’s rainfall volume are bigger concerns, since membrane systems don’t shed water by gravity the way a pitched roof does. We adjust the assessment approach based on roof type, which matters for both homeowners with additions or porches and for the commercial buildings we service across the same storm systems.What's IncludedFull on-roof storm assessment, not a drive-by estimateDamage documentation formatted for insurance adjustersWind, hail, and debris damage repair from the same crews who handle full replacementsStraight answers on repair versus replacement, without steering toward the bigger jobCoordination with your insurance timeline so tarping and permanent repair stay on scheduleFrequently Asked QuestionsHow do I know if a storm actually damaged my roof?Some damage is obvious - missing shingles, visible holes, granules pooling in gutters. A lot of it isn't visible from the ground at all, which is why we recommend a roof inspection after any significant wind or hail event, even if nothing looks wrong from the driveway. Bruised shingles from hail, for instance, often don't leak immediately but fail years earlier than they should.Should I call my insurance company or a roofer first after storm damage?Either order can work, but getting a roofer's assessment first means you walk into the insurance conversation with a clear, documented picture of the damage rather than relying solely on the adjuster's initial read. We're happy to inspect first and hand you a report to bring to your insurer, or to meet the adjuster on-site if you've already filed.Does storm damage always mean a full roof replacement?No. Isolated wind damage - a section of lifted or missing shingles - is often a straightforward repair. Widespread hail bruising across the whole field of the roof, or damage combined with an older roof already near the end of its life, more often points to replacement. We assess and tell you honestly which category your roof falls into.How soon after a storm should I get my roof checked?As soon as it's safe to do so, ideally within a few days. Prompt inspection matters both for catching active leaks before they cause interior damage and because most insurance policies have windows for filing storm-related claims. Photos taken soon after the event also tend to hold up better with adjusters than damage assessed weeks later.What Northeast Ohio storm patterns cause the most roof damage each year?Summer brings fast-developing thunderstorm complexes off the lake that can produce straight-line wind gusts and occasional hail with little warning. Late fall and winter bring wind events tied to lake-effect weather systems, sometimes strong enough to lift ridge caps even without any precipitation involved. We see damage patterns shift with the season, which shapes what we check first during an assessment depending on when the storm happened.Can one storm cause damage that only shows up after a later, smaller storm?Yes, and this is a common and underappreciated pattern. A wind event can loosen fasteners or lift a shingle edge without fully detaching it, leaving a weak point that then fails completely in a much smaller subsequent storm. This is one reason we check the whole roof field after any significant event rather than just the spots with obvious damage - a shingle that's 80 percent failed today is 100 percent failed after the next moderate gust.Related ServicesWind Damage RepairHail Damage RepairInsurance Claims AssistanceMore on Storm Damage RoofingGuides and cost breakdowns related to this service.How to Choose a Contractor for Storm Damage RepairWhat to Do Immediately After Storm Damage to Your RoofHow Ohio Storms and Wind Damage RoofsWhat Hail Damage to a Roof Actually Looks LikeGet Your Free Storm Damage Roofing EstimateTell us about your project and we'll follow up within one business day - no obligation.Prefer to talk it through first?Call (216) 424-3811

Leaks start at seams, at the base of rooftop-unit curbs, at pipes and hatches, at parapet walls and edge metal, and wherever water sits because a drain is clogged or the deck has settled. Finding the entry point on a flat roof is harder than on a pitched roof, because water travels across the deck before it drips.Repairs are matched to the membrane: heat-welded patches on TPO, primed and taped patches on EPDM, and torch or cold-applied patches on modified bitumen. Sealant alone is a temporary measure, and we label it that way on the report.Warning signsSigns a commercial roof needs repairDrips from ceiling tilesWater has been sitting on the deck for a while.Ponding that stays after two daysDrains or slope are not doing their job.Blisters or bubbles in the membraneMoisture or air trapped under the sheet.Open or lifted seamsThe most common leak point on single-ply roofs.Loose edge metal after windWind is getting under the membrane at the perimeter.Cracked flashing at rooftop unitsCurbs move and the flashing tears around them.Debris clogging drains and scuppersWater backs up and finds the weakest seam.Step by stepHow a commercial leak call runs1Answer and dispatchCalls taken 24/7; active leaks get the first crew.2Stop the waterTemporary patch or cover over the entry point.3Trace the leakFrom the interior drip back across the deck to the entry.4Permanent repairMembrane-matched patch, seam weld or flashing rebuild.5ReportPhotos, the cause, and any other risks on the roof.TimelineHow long a commercial repair takesStopping active water is usually a single visit. Most permanent repairs to seams, drains and curbs are finished in a day, weather allowing, once materials matched to the membrane are on hand. Larger problems, such as wet insulation under a section of roof, need a core sample and a scheduled section replacement, and we tell you that on the first visit rather than after several patches.Specific jobs we handleMembrane seam and puncture repairOpen seams and punctures from dropped tools, foot traffic or hail are the most common commercial repairs. We clean and prepare the membrane around the damage, then weld, tape or adhere a patch of the same material, extending well past the damaged area. On TPO, every weld is probed afterward. If a roof has open seams in many places we say so, because at that point a restoration coating or a replacement may cost less than chasing seams one at a time.Ponding water and drain repairWater that stays on a flat roof for more than a day or two after rain adds weight, speeds membrane aging and finds any weak seam. The cause is usually a clogged drain or scupper, a crushed strainer, or a deck that has sagged around the drain. We clear and reset drains, replace damaged drain bowls and clamping rings, and add tapered insulation or crickets where the slope needs correcting, so the water leaves within hours instead of days and stops loading the deck.Flashing at curbs and parapetsRooftop units, exhaust fans and hatches sit on curbs, and the membrane flashing up the curb tears as equipment vibrates and the roof moves. Parapet walls fail at the base flashing and at the coping on top. We rebuild curb flashing with new membrane and termination bars, reseal or replace coping joints, and check that counterflashing covers the top of every flashed wall. It is the most common source of recurring leaks we find on commercial roofs, and the one most often patched with sealant.Around ColumbusWhat this job looks like on Columbus roofsWind is the main threat to flat roofs here. Home Size (Sq Ft)Estimated Roof SizeLow EstimateMid EstimateHigh Estimate1,000 to 1,50018 to 24 squares$8,200$12,800$14,500+1,500 to 2,00022 to 30 squares$9,500$14,500$18,500+2,000 to 2,50028 to 38 squares$11,500$16,500$21,000+2,500 to 3,00035 to 46 squares$14,000$19,500$25,000+3,000 to 3,50042 to 55 squares$16,500$23,000$29,500+ Note on These Ranges A roofing “square” equals 100 square feet of roof surface. Roof square footage is always larger than your home’s footprint because of pitch, overhangs, and the geometry of hips, valleys, and dormers. A 2,000 sq ft ranch home typically has a roof between 24 and 32 squares depending on pitch. What Affects Roofing Costs in the Cleveland Market Roof Pitch Pitch is one of the biggest cost variables in Cleveland. A low-slope roof (4/12 or less) is faster and safer to work on. A steep roof (8/12 or above) requires safety equipment, slower installation, and more labor hours. Steep pitch typically adds $1.00 to $2.50 per square foot to the total project cost. Many older Craftsman, Victorian, and Colonial homes in Cleveland Heights, Lakewood, and Westlake have steeper pitches that push projects toward the top of the range. Number of Layers Being Removed Ohio residential code allows a maximum of two layers of asphalt shingles on a roof. If your home already has two layers, both must come off before a new roof can be installed. That tear-off adds $1,000 to $2,500 to your project depending on roof size and disposal costs. If you have only one layer, tear-off is included in most standard estimates. Decking Condition Your roof deck is the plywood or OSB sheathing under your shingles. When a Cleveland contractor tears off your old roof, damaged or rotted decking sections must be replaced before new shingles go down. Deck repairs are typically priced per sheet at $75 to $150 per 4×8 sheet installed. Minor deck damage on an average Cleveland home adds $200 to $600. Extensive rot from chronic ice dam damage can add $1,500 or more. Your contractor should not know the full extent of deck damage until tear-off is complete, so ask how they handle decking discoveries mid-project. Shingle Material and Grade The shingle you choose has a significant impact on total cost. Here is a current comparison for the Cleveland market: Shingle TypeInstalled Cost Per SquareExpected Lifespan in OhioNotes3-Tab Asphalt$250 to $35015 to 20 yearsBudget option; declining in popularity; limited warrantyArchitectural (Dimensional)$350 to $50025 to 30 yearsMost popular in Cleveland; best value for most homeownersClass 4 Impact-Resistant$450 to $60025 to 35 yearsRecommended for Northeast Ohio; may qualify for insurance discountMetal (Steel Standing Seam)$1,200 to $1,80040 to 60 yearsHigh upfront cost; lowest lifetime cost; excellent for Ohio wintersCedar Shake$800 to $1,20020 to 30 yearsAesthetic appeal; higher maintenance requirement in Ohio climateSynthetic Slate$800 to $1,20030 to 50 yearsLighter than real slate; good freeze-thaw performance Ventilation and Underlayment A complete roof system is more than shingles. Proper attic ventilation is critical in Northeast Ohio to prevent ice dams, extend shingle life, and maintain your manufacturer warranty. If your current ventilation is inadequate, adding or upgrading ridge vents, soffit vents, or box vents will add $300 to $800 to your project. Ice and water shield underlayment is required by Ohio code at the eaves and is standard on any legitimate estimate. Synthetic underlayment across the full deck is a worthwhile upgrade over felt paper in Ohio’s climate. Flashing and Accessories Properly installed flashing around chimneys, skylights, vents, and in valleys is where most roof leaks originate. If your chimney flashing is failing, step flashing needs replacement, or you have a large masonry chimney that requires re-flashing, budget an additional $300 to $1,200 depending on complexity. These are not optional items on a quality installation. Cleveland-Specific Roof Replacement Cost Factors A few factors make Cleveland pricing somewhat different from national averages: Labor market: Northeast Ohio has a competitive but not extreme roofing labor market. Installed costs here tend to run 5 to 10 percent below Chicago or Columbus prices for equivalent work. Permit costs: Most Cleveland-area municipalities require a permit for roof replacement. Permit costs range from $75 to $300 depending on the municipality (Cleveland, Parma, Westlake, Strongsville, and others all have different fee schedules). A legitimate contractor pulls the permit on your behalf and includes this cost. Disposal and landfill fees: Cuyahoga County landfill tip fees for roofing tear-off material are factored into contractor pricing. Projects with two-layer tear-offs generate significantly more debris weight. Ice and water shield code requirements: Ohio code requires ice and water shield to extend from the eave to at least 24 inches inside the interior wall line, measured along the roof slope. In Cleveland’s climate, most reputable contractors go well beyond this minimum, commonly running ice and water shield 36 to 48 inches or more up the deck from the eave to protect against the severe ice dam conditions created by Lake Erie’s snow belt. What a Legitimate Cleveland Roofing Estimate Should Include When you receive an estimate, it should itemize all of these components. If a contractor gives you a single lump-sum number without breaking out materials and labor, ask for clarification before signing anything. Tear-off of existing shingles (number of layers specified) Disposal and haul-away of all debris New drip edge on all eaves and rakes Ice and water shield at eaves (footage specified) Synthetic underlayment across full deck Starter strip shingles at all eaves and rakes Shingle brand, product line, and color Ridge cap shingles (not cut shingles) Ventilation assessment and any upgrades needed Flashing replacement or reuse (specified per location) Permit fees Workmanship warranty terms (length and what is covered) NOTE: The Lowest Bid Is Not Always the Best Value In the Cleveland market, we consistently see low-bid contractors skip or use inferior versions of several line items above: using felt paper instead of synthetic underlayment, reusing old flashing instead of replacing it, cutting ridge cap shingles from field shingles instead of using manufacturer ridge cap product, and skipping the permit entirely. These shortcuts save $400 to $800 on the estimate but void your manufacturer warranty and create liability for you as the homeowner. Does Insurance Cover Roof Replacement in Cleveland? If your roof was damaged by a qualifying storm event (hail, wind, fallen tree), your homeowners insurance policy may cover most or all of the replacement cost minus your deductible. Greater Cleveland and Cuyahoga County see significant hail and wind damage every year. If your roof is 15 years old or newer and you have experienced a storm in the past 12 months, a professional roof inspection is worth doing before you assume you are paying out of pocket. Python Roofing provides free storm damage inspections and will tell you honestly whether we see claimable damage. We work directly with insurance adjusters and handle the documentation process for you. Helpful Articles Does Homeowners Insurance Cover Roof Replacement in Ohio? (By Material and Climate) Cleveland Roof Cost FAQs What is the average cost to replace a roof in Cleveland, Ohio in 2026? Most Cleveland homeowners with a standard 1,500 to 2,500 sq ft home pay between $10,000 and $14,500 for a full roof replacement using architectural asphalt shingles. Smaller homes can come in below $10,000. Larger homes with steep pitches, multiple layers to remove, or premium materials can exceed $20,000. How long does a roof replacement take in Cleveland? Most standard single-family roof replacements in Cleveland take one to two days for the full crew to complete. Larger homes, steep pitches, or significant decking repairs can extend the timeline to two to three days. Weather delays are always possible in Northeast Ohio. See our full walkthrough post on what to expect during a roof replacement. Is a building permit required for roof replacement in Cleveland? Yes, most Cleveland-area municipalities require a permit for a full roof replacement. Your contractor should pull the permit on your behalf. If a contractor tells you a permit is not required or suggests skipping it to save money, that is a red flag. Can I get financing for a roof replacement in Cleveland? Yes. https://ohiofirstchoiceroofing.com/guide.text: Roofing guideWhat a new roof costs in Columbus in 2026, and why quotes differPublished figures for a new roof in Columbus run from $5,688 to $16,000 for a typical house. The spread is not random; it follows the size of the roof, what is under the old shingles and what the quote actually includes. Call (380) 888-0187All guides Answered 24/7 Columbus roofers Written for homeownersWritten by Beverly Underhill, Roofing Guides Author. Updated September 2026Most full roof replacements in Columbus fall between $5,688 and $12,760 according to Angi's 2026 data, with an average of $9,068; local contractors' 2026 figures for a 2,000 square foot asphalt roof run from $9,000 to $16,000, and size, pitch, layers, decking and the shingle line decide where a roof lands.The numbers published for 2026Three sets of figures are worth knowing. Angi's Columbus data, updated in August 2026, puts most replacements between $5,688 and $12,760, with an average of $9,068, and estimates the labor share at $4,500 to $5,450. Fixr's statewide figures put an Ohio replacement at $6,000 to $12,000, with about $7,500 typical for a 2,000 square foot roof in mid-grade architectural shingles.Local roofers publishing 2026 pricing land higher. One Columbus contractor puts a 2,000 square foot asphalt roof at $9,000 to $16,000 installed with tear-off, and another quotes $8,500 to $13,500 for a 1,700 to 2,000 square foot home.The gap has a reason. National data sites average many jobs, including small and simple roofs, while local contractors price the roofs they actually see, and in Columbus that includes a lot of older houses with harder tear-offs. Treat every one of these figures as a planning range. None of them is a quote, including anything on this site.How roofers price a roofRoofers measure in squares; one square covers 100 square feet of roof surface. A typical single-family house in the area has somewhere between 15 and 30 squares once pitch and overhangs are counted, which is more than the house's footprint suggests. Published 2026 figures for asphalt run $4.50 to $8.00 per square foot with tear-off included, or about $5 on average.Pitch changes the math. Steep roofs need harnesses, roof jacks and slower work, and every valley, dormer and chimney adds cutting and flashing. A cut-up roof of the same area can cost noticeably more than a simple gable, which is why two houses on the same street rarely get the same price.What pushes a Columbus roof to the top of the rangeLayers. Ohio code requires a replacement to strip the existing coverings down to the deck, so a roof with two or three old layers costs more to tear off. Angi puts tear-off and disposal at around $1,000 for asphalt and up to $3,000 for heavier materials like slate or tile.Decking. Half of Ohio's housing was built before 1965, and older houses often have plank decking with gaps, or sheathing softened by old leaks. One local 2026 guide puts decking damage and complex geometry at $1,000 to $3,000 on top of a quote.Code items. The eaves need an ice barrier running at least 24 inches inside the wall line, and new flashing, drip edge and ventilation belong on every replacement. Quotes that leave these out look cheaper and are not describing the same roof.Historic districts. In German Village and the other districts, an approval step and approved materials can add both cost and time.Materials and what they costAsphalt shingles are the most common roof in Columbus at about $5 per square foot installed, while metal runs about $11 per square foot and lasts roughly twice as long, according to Angi. Exterior Alliance's 2026 figures put three-tab shingles at $3.50 to $5.00 per square foot, architectural at $4.00 to $8.50 and standing seam metal at $10 to $23, with a full metal roof on a typical house at $18,000 to $35,000 or more.For most houses, architectural shingles are the value choice. Metal makes sense if you plan to stay long enough for its lifespan to pay back the higher price. Clay, concrete and slate are far less common in Ohio and cost more again.Need a roofer while you read this?Want a written price for your own roof instead of a range? Call and we will measure it. Call (380) 888-0187What insurance pays and what it does notIf a covered storm damaged the roof, a homeowner's policy usually pays for the replacement minus the deductible; normal age and wear are not covered. Some policies pay actual cash value, which depreciates an older roof, while others pay full replacement cost. Code items like ice barrier may or may not be covered, depending on your policy's code-upgrade coverage.Read the policy, and get the roof documented before you file. The insurance claim roof page covers how that documentation is put together.How to compare two quotesPut the quotes side by side and check each line: tear-off to the deck and disposal, decking priced per sheet, drip edge, ice barrier at the eaves and valleys, the underlayment type, new step and valley flashing rather than reused, pipe boots, ventilation, the shingle line by name, and cleanup. A quote missing half of those lines is not cheaper; it is describing a different roof.Ask what happens if soft decking is found and how it is priced before you sign. That one question settles more disputes than any other.Questions we getRoof cost questionsHow much does a roof replacement cost in Columbus in 2026? Angi's 2026 data puts most at $5,688 to $12,760, averaging $9,068. Local contractors' figures for a 2,000 square foot asphalt roof run about $9,000 to $16,000.Why are local quotes higher than national averages? Averages include small, simple roofs. Older Columbus houses often need more tear-off and decking work.Can I save money by roofing over the old shingles? Not on a replacement. Ohio code requires removing existing coverings to the deck.Is metal worth the extra cost? It costs roughly twice as much per square foot as asphalt and lasts roughly twice as long, so it pays back if you stay.Does insurance pay for a new roof? Only when a covered peril such as hail or wind damaged it, minus your deductible.Related workServices this guide coversRoof ReplacementFull tear-off to the deck.See the service Asphalt Shingle RoofingArchitectural shingles.See the service Metal RoofingStanding seam panels.See the service Keep readingMore roofing guidesHail Damage and Your Roof Insurance Claim in OhioHow hail bruising is documented and how a claim actually runs in Ohio.Read the guide Reroofing in German Village: How the Approval WorksThe approval step, approved materials and how long it adds.Read the guide Metal vs Asphalt Shingles for a Columbus HomeCost, lifespan, snow and hail compared for a Columbus house.Read the guide Call any hourWant a real number for your roof?Call and we will measure the roof, check the deck from the attic and give you a written price with every line item. Wind damage shows as creased shingles and lifted tabs along the windward edge. Both are easy to miss from the ground, which is why insurers so often want photographs from on the roof.We inspect free after any significant storm and you keep the photographs whether you claim, hire us, or do nothing at all. In winter the same call is usually about ice dams, which are a ventilation problem wearing a weather problem's clothes.The insurance partCarriers in this county see a lot of hail claims and scrutinize them accordingly. The two things that decide a claim are documentation and timing, photographs taken close to the storm date, and a claim filed before the policy window closes.We will meet the adjuster on the roof with you. Not to argue, but because an adjuster looking at a roof alone from a ladder sees less than one being shown where the bruising is. That is usually the whole difference between a repair settlement and a replacement settlement.Frequently asked questionsHow do I know if my roof has hail damage?+Look for circular marks where the grit has been knocked away, showing the darker layer beneath, often easier to feel than see. Dented gutters, downspouts or air conditioner fins are the giveaway from the ground: if the soft metal is dented, the roof took the same hit. Get it looked at within a few weeks of the storm, because claims get harder to argue as the evidence weathers.Will my insurance cover storm damage to my roof?+Usually, if the damage is genuinely storm-related and the claim is filed inside the policy window. What carriers push back on is age. They will argue a worn roof failed on its own. That is why photographs dated close to the storm matter, and why we take them whether or not you have decided to claim.How long do I have to file a roof claim in Ohio?+Most Ohio policies give you one to two years from the date of the storm. In practice the window is much shorter, because the evidence weathers. An adjuster treats a six-month-old claim very differently from a six-week-old one. If a storm has been through, get it inspected now even if you do nothing with the report.Do you tarp roofs after a storm?+Yes, and same-night where we can. A tarp is not a repair, it is a way of stopping water getting into the ceiling while the weather clears and the claim gets sorted. See emergency roof repair.Free EstimateGet the damage documented while it still countsFree, on the roof, and the file is yours whether you claim, hire us, or do neither.Storm just been through? # How Much Does Gutter Replacement Cost in Dayton, Ohio?

What you'll actually pay depends on your specific home. Here's everything that affects the investment — so you can get quotes with confidence.

  1.  
  2.  
  3. Gutter Replacement Cost Dayton
One of the most common questions we hear from Dayton homeowners is: “How much is this going to cost me?” It's a completely fair question — but the honest answer is that gutter replacement cost varies significantly based on your specific home.

Rather than throwing out a number that might not reflect your situation, we think it's more helpful to walk you through everything that drives that cost. That way, when you get quotes from contractors, you'll understand exactly what you're paying for — and why.
The best way to find out what new gutters will cost for your home in Dayton, Kettering, Centerville, Miamisburg, Beavercreek, or anywhere in Southwest Ohio is to get a free on-site estimate from a local professional.
### On this page

  *

  *  
  *  
  *  

## 8 Factors That Affect Gutter Replacement Cost

Every home is different. These are the variables contractors evaluate when building your quote.
### Home Size & Linear Footage

The total length of gutter run needed is the biggest cost driver. Larger homes with more roofline coverage naturally require more material and labor time.

### Stories & Roof Pitch

Two-story homes and steep rooflines require more safety equipment, additional labor, and longer setup time — all of which affect the final investment.
### Gutter Material Choice

Aluminum is the most popular option in Ohio for its durability and resistance to rust. Copper and steel are also available at different price points.

### Gutter Size (5" vs 6")

Six-inch gutters handle more water volume and are recommended for steeper roofs or areas with heavy rainfall. They typically cost a bit more than standard 5-inch gutters.
### Gutter Guard Addition

Adding gutter guards at the time of installation can be more cost-effective than installing them separately later. Guards vary widely by type and quality.

### Old Gutter Removal

If your old gutters need to be removed and disposed of before new ones go up, that adds to the overall scope of work.

### Fascia & Soffit Condition

If the wood behind your gutters is rotted or damaged, it needs to be repaired before installation. Skipping this step leads to premature gutter failure.
### Your Location in the Dayton Area

Travel distance, local labor rates, and regional demand can all slightly affect what contractors quote in different parts of Southwest Ohio.
## Why We Don't List Prices Here

You'll find plenty of websites that throw out generic price ranges or national averages. The problem? Those numbers don't account for your home's layout, your local labor market, or current material costs.

We believe the most honest thing we can do is give you an accurate free estimate for your home — not a range so wide it's nearly useless. That's exactly what our free on-site consultations are for.
## What to Ask When Getting Quotes

Is this a seamless or sectional gutter installation?

What gutter material and gauge are you using?

Does this include removal and disposal of my old gutters?

Will you inspect and repair the fascia board if needed?

What warranty do you offer on labor and materials?

Are you licensed, insured, and local to Dayton?

## Frequently Asked Questions
### Does homeowner's insurance cover gutter replacement?

Insurance typically covers gutter damage caused by sudden events like storm damage or fallen trees, but not normal wear and aging. Contact your insurer to review your specific policy.

### How long do new gutters last?

Properly installed aluminum seamless gutters in Ohio typically last 20 to 30 years with minimal maintenance. Copper gutters can last 50 years or more.
### Is it worth getting seamless gutters over sectional?

For most Dayton homeowners, yes. Seamless gutters have fewer joints, which means fewer leak points. They also tend to look cleaner and hold up better over time.

### How do I know if I just need repair vs full replacement?

Minor issues like a single leak or loose hanger can often be repaired. If you have widespread sagging, significant rust, pulling away from the fascia, or gutters over 20 years old, replacement is usually the smarter investment.

The only way to know what gutter replacement will actually cost for your home is to have a local expert take a look. We offer free, no-pressure consultations throughout Dayton and Southwest Ohio.

04 — Good to Know
## Questions, Answered

Do you offer free estimates or consultations?

Yes, we offer 100% free, no-obligation estimates. One of our experienced team members will visit your property, assess the area, and provide a customized quote based on your needs and preferences.

What types of materials do you offer for decks and fences?
We work with a wide range of materials including pressure-treated wood, composite decking, cedar, vinyl, and aluminum. We'll help you choose the right option based on durability, budget, and aesthetics.

Can you customize the design of my deck or fence?

Absolutely. Every property is different, and we take pride in creating custom solutions that fit your space and vision. Whether you're looking for a modern deck design or a privacy fence with unique detailing, we'll work with you to bring it to life.
How long does it typically take to complete a fence or deck project?

Project timelines can vary based on size, design, and materials, but most residential fences are completed in 2-4 days, while decks may take 1-2 weeks. We provide a clear schedule before starting so you know exactly what to expect.

Is your work covered by a warranty?
Yes. Every completed installation carries a 1-year warranty on our workmanship and the materials we supply, and standard manufacturer warranties on the products pass through to you. It does not cover normal weathering, acts of nature, misuse, alterations made after installation, and damage caused by a third party.

# Storm Damage Repair Done Right

We restore roofs, siding, and gutters fast while helping you through the insurance claim process.

[Button: Get in touch] Call Us
                  
### Service Details

When a storm hits, roof damage is not always easy to spot from the ground. We help homeowners in Delaware County, OH find the problem fast, stop active leaks, and make a clear plan for repair. At Myers Roofing And Siding, storm damage repair means more than patching a few shingles. We inspect the full roofing system, look for hidden damage, and guide you through what needs to happen next so you can protect your home and avoid bigger problems.
Storms can damage a roof in several ways. High winds can lift or tear off shingles. Hail can bruise roofing materials, crack shingle surfaces, and shorten the life of the roof. Heavy rain can push water under damaged areas and lead to leaks, wood rot, mold, or ceiling stains. Siding and gutters can also take a hit during severe weather, which is why we look at the exterior as a whole instead of focusing on one visible issue.
## What our storm damage repair service includes
We start with a detailed inspection of the roof, flashing, vents, ridge caps, valleys, gutters, and siding. We check for missing shingles, lifted tabs, hail impact marks, granule loss, soft spots, punctures, dented metal components, and water entry points. If there is interior leaking, we also pay attention to signs like wet insulation, attic moisture, and staining on walls or ceilings. This helps us understand both the direct damage and any secondary issues caused by the storm.
After the inspection, we explain what we found in simple terms. If the damage is minor, we may recommend targeted roof repairs to restore the affected area and help extend the life of the existing roof. If the storm damage is widespread or the roofing system has been compromised beyond a practical repair, we will explain that clearly and discuss replacement options. Our goal is to give you honest guidance based on the condition of your home, not a one-size-fits-all sales pitch.
## Common storm-related repairs

  * Replacing missing, torn, or creased asphalt shingles
  * Repairing roof leaks and sealing vulnerable areas
  * Replacing damaged flashing around chimneys, walls, and roof penetrations
  * Fixing hail-damaged ridge caps, vents, and other roofing components
  * Addressing damage to gutters, downspouts, and siding
  * Correcting water intrusion that started after wind or hail events
  * Emergency tarping or temporary protection when needed to limit further damage
## Why fast storm damage repair matters

Even small storm damage can turn into a much larger repair if it is left alone. A loose shingle can lead to a leak. A leak can soak the roof deck, attic insulation, drywall, and framing. Water intrusion can also create conditions for mold growth and indoor air quality issues. Fast action helps lower the risk of more costly structural damage and can improve the chances of a smoother insurance claim by documenting the condition early.
## Insurance claim support from an experienced restoration contractor

One of the biggest parts of storm damage repair is dealing with the insurance process. Many homeowners are unsure what to do first, what to document, or how to talk with their carrier. Myers Roofing And Siding is proud to be a leading insurance restoration roofing contractor serving Delaware County, Ohio. We guide and advocate for you during the claim process so you are not left trying to figure it out alone.
We help document storm-related damage, provide clear findings, and explain the repair scope in a way that supports the restoration process. Our team understands how wind damage, hail damage, and related exterior damage are commonly evaluated. That experience helps us communicate clearly and keep the process moving. We want you to feel informed at every step, from the first inspection to the final repair.
## Our process
  1. Inspection: We assess the roof, gutters, siding, and visible storm impact areas.
  2. Documentation: We record the damage and note repair or replacement needs.
  3. Recommendations: We explain your options and the best path forward for your home.
  4. Claim guidance: If insurance is involved, we help you understand the process and next steps.
  5. Repair work: We complete the storm damage repairs using quality materials and proven methods.
  6. Final review: We make sure the work is complete and your home is protected.
## What makes our team different
Storm damage restoration is not just about construction. It is also about communication, timing, and trust. We know this can be a stressful situation, especially when water is getting in or you are worried about what insurance will cover. We take a practical, straightforward approach. We show up, inspect carefully, explain what we see, and do the work the right way.
Because we also handle roofing, gutters, and siding, we can address multiple storm-related issues without sending you to several different contractors.
We also understand local weather patterns and the kinds of damage homes in Delaware County, OH often face after wind storms, hail storms, and heavy rain. That local knowledge helps us spot issues that are easy to miss and recommend repairs that fit the real condition of the property.
## Signs you may need storm damage repair

  * Shingles on the ground after a storm
  * Water spots on ceilings or walls
  * Leaks in the attic or around vents
  * Dented gutters, flashing, or metal roof parts
  * Granules collecting in gutters or downspouts
  * Cracked, bruised, or lifted shingles
  * Siding panels that are loose, cracked, or broken
If you have noticed any of these warning signs, or if your home has recently been through a strong storm, it is smart to schedule an inspection right away. Some damage is obvious, but some only shows up after water has already started getting in.

Exterior Painting Questions How much does it cost to paint the exterior of a house in Columbus, Ohio? Most exterior painting projects in Columbus range from $3,000 to $8,000 depending on home size, number of stories, siding material, and how much prep work is needed. A single-story ranch with clean siding falls on the low end. A two-story home with peeling paint, rot repair, and multiple substrates falls on the high end. Square footage, accessibility, and coat count all factor in. We provide detailed written estimates that break down labor, materials, prep and repairs, and coat count. No hidden fees and no deposit required. Call 614-582-4227 or request a free estimate above. How long does exterior paint last in Ohio? With proper prep and quality products, exterior paint on wood siding and trim typically lasts 7 to 10 years in Central Ohio. Fiber cement and LP SmartSide hold paint longer, often 12 to 15 years. Vinyl siding that's been painted with a vinyl-safe formula can last 5 to 7 years depending on sun exposure and color choice. The biggest factor isn't the paint. It's the prep underneath it. Skipped caulking, bare wood left unprimed, and paint applied over chalk are why most exterior jobs fail early. That's why we spend more time on prep work than most contractors. What are the signs my house needs to be repainted? The most common signs are peeling or flaking paint, chalking (white powder when you rub the surface), faded or uneven color between sun-exposed and shaded sides, cracked or missing caulk around windows and trim, and visible bare wood. If you see any of these, moisture is likely getting behind the paint film and causing damage you can't see yet. Catching it early saves money. A repaint with minor prep costs significantly less than a project that includes siding repairs, rot replacement, and carpentry work. We offer free exterior inspections. Call 614-582-4227. Should I repair or replace exterior trim before painting? Always. Painting over damaged trim is the most common shortcut we see, and it's why so many exterior paint jobs fail within two years. If trim is soft, split, or pulling away from the house, paint won't fix it. Moisture is already behind the surface and will keep pushing the new coating off. Minor surface damage can be filled and sanded, but anything with rot, water damage, or structural compromise needs to be cut out and replaced with solid material before primer goes on. The problem is most painters don't do carpentry, so they either skip it, patch over it, or tell you to call someone else first. That's where the project stalls. As a licensed general contractor, we handle trim replacement, siding repairs, and painting under one roof. One crew, one schedule, no waiting on a second contractor to show up. Can you paint the exterior of a house in cold weather? Yes, but with conditions. Most exterior paints need air and surface temperatures above 50°F, with no rain in the forecast for at least 24 hours. Some products like Benjamin Moore Aura Exterior can be applied in temperatures as low as 35°F, which extends our painting season into late fall and early spring in Central Ohio. We monitor the forecast daily and won't apply finish coats if conditions aren't right for proper cure. Painting in marginal weather to stay on schedule is how most exterior failures happen. We'd rather push a project a few days than put a coat down that peels by March. If you're planning an exterior project, late spring through early fall gives us the widest window for consistent results. Does exterior painting increase home value? Yes, and it's one of the highest-ROI home improvements you can make. Industry data consistently shows exterior painting returns 50% or more on investment. In a competitive market like Columbus, fresh curb appeal can be the difference between a showing and a passed listing. Buyers notice peeling paint, faded siding, and neglected trim before they even walk through the front door. A pre-sale exterior repaint doesn't always mean the whole house. Sometimes it's the trim, fascia, front door, and shutters that make the biggest visual impact. We can walk your home and tell you exactly where the money is best spent. See our full residential painting services or call 614-582-4227. Should I paint or replace my siding? If the siding is structurally sound with no rot, no warping, and no widespread cracking, painting is almost always the better investment. A quality exterior paint job on solid siding costs a fraction of full replacement and can buy you another 7 to 10 years. If the siding is failing in isolated areas, we can replace damaged sections and paint the rest to match. If the damage is widespread with rot through multiple courses, vinyl that's cracking and buckling, or aluminum that's dented beyond repair, replacement makes more sense long-term. We install Hardie Board, LP SmartSide, and vinyl siding in addition to painting. As a licensed general contractor, we'll give you an honest recommendation either way. Do I need to be home while my house is being painted? No. Most of our exterior projects happen while homeowners are at work. All the work is outside, so we don't need interior access unless you're also doing an interior repaint at the same time. We communicate the daily plan by text or phone, send progress photos, and schedule the final walkthrough when you're available. We just ask that vehicles are moved away from the house, pets are kept inside during work hours, and we have access to an exterior outlet and water spigot. Everything else, including masking, protection, landscaping coverage, and cleanup, we handle. Get a Free Quote

### Signs You Need Ice Dam Removal

Recognizing the early warning signs of ice dams can save you thousands in repair costs and prevent serious structural damage to your Columbus home. Ice dams form when heated air from your home melts snow on the roof, which then refreezes at the colder eaves, creating a barrier that traps water. If you notice any of these symptoms, it’s crucial to contact Imperial Roofing immediately for professional ice dam removal before the problem worsens:
  * Large icicles hanging from eaves
  * Water stains on ceilings or walls
  * Leaks during winter thaws

  * Gutters sagging under ice weight
  * Persistent attic moisture or mold
  * Snow melting unevenly on roof

## FAQs About Ice Dam Removal

How quickly can you respond?

We offer fast scheduling and often same-day service during peak ice dam season.

Will steam damage my shingles?

No—our low-pressure steam safely melts ice without harming shingles, gutters, or flashing.

Do you remove ice from gutters, too?

Yes, we clear both your roof and gutters to restore full drainage.

Can you help with insurance claims?
 Absolutely. We provide photos, reports, and estimates to simplify your claim and speed up approvals.

Do you guarantee your work?

Yes, all work is backed by our workmanship warranty.
## Preventing Future Ice Dam Problems

Removing the ice is only half the solution; preventing it from coming back is just as important. After completing your ice dam removal, we inspect your roof and attic to pinpoint what caused the problem, such as inadequate insulation, poor ventilation, or warm air leaks into the attic. These issues allow snow to melt unevenly and refreeze at the roof edge.
We use thermal imaging and moisture detection tools to identify hidden problem areas, then provide clear recommendations for targeted improvements. By sealing air leaks, improving insulation, or adding , we can help prevent future ice dam formation altogether. Taking these proactive steps not only protects your roof from damage but also improves your home’s energy efficiency and indoor comfort.

  
### Our Ice Dam Removal Process

Our process begins with a safety setup and roof inspection to map the location and size of the ice dam. We use commercial-grade steamers to melt ice gently, working from the lower edge upward to avoid water intrusion. Steam loosens the bond between the ice and the roof without damaging shingles or gutters. As we clear the ice, we continuously remove meltwater to keep your roof dry.
After the dam is fully removed, we inspect for leaks, water-damaged decking, or loose flashing that may need attention. Finally, we provide a written report and photos for your records or insurance claim. This methodical, safety-first approach ensures your ice dam is removed thoroughly and without harm to your roofing system.
